cards.when: 처음 이야기에 올리는 사람 · 물건
cards.en: There is a cat over there.

cards.when: 눈앞에서 일어난 일
cards.en: Wow, it is snowing!

cards.when: 누가 했는지가 새 정보
cards.en: Who came? Minsu did.

cards.when: 「-아서/어서」 앞 문장의 주어
cards.en: I was late because it rained.

cards.when: 이 두 말 앞의 말에는 이/가
cards.en: I am not a doctor. / I want to become a doctor.

split.en: There is a student over there.
Oh, it is raining!
Jiyoung came.
The road is slippery because it snowed.
split.note: 한 문장에 조사가 둘이면 조사 블록도 둘

choose.en: There is a cat over there.
choose.why: 고양이 ends in a vowel, so 가.

choose.en: Who came? Minsu did.
choose.why: 수 ends in a vowel, so 가.

choose.en: I am not a doctor.
choose.why: 아니다 needs 이/가 before it, and 사 is a vowel, so 가.

choose.en: The sky is blue. The clouds are white.
choose.why: 하늘 and 구름 both end in a consonant, so 이 · 이.

fill.en: I was glad because a friend came.

cards.when: 무엇에 대해 이야기할지 화제를 꺼낼 때
cards.en: I am Sujin.

cards.when: 둘을 서로 견주어 다름을 나타낼 때
cards.en: Apples are sweet, but lemons are sour.

cards.when: 세상 누구나 아는 성질이나 사실을 말할 때
cards.en: Cheetahs are fast.

cards.when: 다른 것은 몰라도 이것만큼은 그렇다고 할 때
cards.en: Today at least, I am busy.

split.en: Minsu is tall.
My older sister is a student.
This bag is really heavy.
My younger sibling is kind.

choose.en: The teacher is kind.
choose.why: 선생님 ends in a consonant, so 은.

choose.q: 지영 씨는 무엇을 해요? 저___ 책을 읽어요.
choose.en: What does Jiyoung do? As for me, I read a book.
choose.why: 저 ends in a vowel, so 는.

choose.en: Winter is cold, but summer is hot.
choose.why: Contrasting winter with summer requires the topic marker 은.

choose.en: Watermelons are big, but grapes are small.
choose.why: 수박 ends in a consonant (은) and 포도 ends in a vowel (는).

cards.when: 무엇을 하는지 동작이 닿는 대상을 밝힐 때
cards.en: I drink water every morning.

cards.when: 좋아하거나 싫어하는 대상을 말할 때
cards.en: I like apples.

cards.when: 무엇을 배우거나 읽는지 나타낼 때
cards.en: Jiyoung learns Korean.

cards.when: 물건을 사거나 팔 때
cards.en: I bought bread at the store.

split.en: Minsu writes a letter.
I eat breakfast.
My friend watches a movie.
I read books diligently.

choose.en: I drink milk.
choose.why: 우유 ends in a vowel, so 를.

choose.en: What do you eat? I eat rice.
choose.why: 밥 ends in a consonant, so 을.

choose.en: Minsu washes the apple.
choose.why: 사과 is the object being washed, so 를.

choose.q: 지영이는 신문___ 읽고 민수는 차___ 마셔요.
choose.en: Jiyoung reads the newspaper, and Minsu drinks tea.
choose.why: 신문 ends in a consonant (을) and 차 ends in a vowel (를).

cards.when: 누구의 물건인지 소유를 나타낼 때
cards.en: This is Minsu's bag.

cards.when: 가족이나 친구 사이의 관계를 말할 때
cards.en: Jiyoung's younger sibling is cute.

cards.when: 어느 곳에 속해 있는지 나타낼 때
cards.en: The number of students at our school is large.

cards.when: 고유한 특성이나 배경을 꾸밀 때
cards.en: Korea's autumn sky is high.

split.en: Here is my friend's house.
My mother's glasses are clean.
I read teacher's letter.
Sujin's shoes are white.

choose.en: These are mother's clothes.
choose.why: Showing possession 'mother's' takes the possessive marker 의.

choose.en: Whose umbrella is it? It is Minsu's umbrella.
choose.why: Answering whose umbrella it is requires the possessive marker 의.

choose.en: My younger sibling's hat is really pretty.
choose.why: Modifying the hat belonging to sibling takes 의.

choose.en: My friend's name is Sujin.
choose.why: 'Friend's name' uses 의, and 이름 as the topic takes 은.

cards.when: 사람이나 사물이 어디에 있는지 말할 때 (있다/없다)
cards.en: There is a book on the desk.

cards.when: 살다, 머물다와 함께 머무르는 장소를 나타낼 때
cards.en: My family lives in Seoul.

cards.when: 몇 시, 무슨 요일 등 일이 일어나는 시간을 가리킬 때
cards.en: I wake up at seven in the morning.

cards.when: 주말이나 특정 날짜를 지정할 때
cards.en: Let's meet on Saturday.

split.en: My friend is in the room.
There are no apples in the refrigerator.
I eat lunch at twelve o'clock.
My younger sibling sleeps at night.

choose.en: The teacher is in the classroom.
choose.why: Indicating static location with 계시다/있다 takes 에.

choose.en: At what time shall we meet?
choose.why: A specific time of an event takes the time marker 에.

choose.en: The wallet is inside the bag.
choose.why: Static location where an object exists takes 에.

choose.en: I am at home on Sunday.
choose.why: Both the time (일요일) and the static existence place (집) take 에.

cards.when: 가다, 오다와 함께 목적지를 나타낼 때
cards.en: I go to school every morning.

cards.when: 집이나 고향으로 돌아올 때
cards.en: I came home in the evening.

cards.when: 수량이나 개수당 기준을 말할 때
cards.en: Apples are 1,000 won each.

cards.when: 하루나 일주일 동안 몇 번 하는지 셀 때
cards.en: I drink water often in a day.

split.en: Minsu went to the park.
Sujin comes to the company.
Watermelon is 10,000 won for one.
I read three books in a week.

choose.en: Where are you going? I drop by the market.
choose.why: Destination with movement takes the direction marker 에.

choose.en: Eggs are 3,000 won for ten.
choose.why: Marking price per unit of count takes 에.

choose.en: Jiyoung entered the library.
choose.why: Entering into a destination takes 에.

choose.en: I go to the hospital twice a day.
choose.why: The first 에 marks frequency per day, and the second marks hospital as destination.

cards.when: 무엇을 먹거나 배우는 구체적인 행동을 할 때
cards.en: I eat a meal at a restaurant.

cards.when: 도서관이나 회사에서 활동할 때
cards.en: I study for the exam at the library.

cards.when: 어디에서 출발하여 오는지 나타낼 때
cards.en: The plane came from America.

cards.when: 어느 나라나 고향에서 왔는지 소개할 때
cards.en: I came from Korea.

split.en: Minsu bought shoes at the market.
I met a friend at the cafe.
My younger sibling reads a book in the room.
I ran diligently in the park.

choose.en: Sujin watches a movie at the theater.
choose.why: The dynamic action of watching a movie at a location takes 에서.

choose.en: Where do you depart from? I depart from Seoul Station.
choose.why: Starting point of departure takes 에서.

choose.en: I borrowed a book at the library.
choose.why: Borrowing a book is an action that takes place at a location, taking 에서.

choose.en: I rest at home and drink coffee at a cafe.
choose.why: Both resting and drinking coffee are active events happening at locations, taking 에서.

fill.en: I bought bread at the bakery.

cards.when: 어디에서 시작하여 어디까지 가는지 거리를 말할 때
cards.en: I walk from home to work.

cards.when: 언제부터 언제까지 시간이 걸리는지 나타낼 때
cards.en: I work from nine o'clock to six o'clock.

cards.when: 월요일부터 금요일처럼 요일 범위를 말할 때
cards.en: There are classes from Monday to Friday.

cards.when: 한 도시에서 다른 도시까지 이동할 때
cards.en: I take a train from Seoul to Busan.

split.en: It takes ten minutes from my house to school.
I studied from one o'clock to three o'clock.
The festival is held from today to tomorrow.
I walked from the station to the park.

choose.en: We start the meeting from ten in the morning.
choose.why: Starting point in time takes 부터.

choose.q: 어디___ 어디까지 가요? 서울에서 대전까지 가요.
choose.en: From where to where are you going? From Seoul to Daejeon.
choose.why: Starting point in physical location takes 에서.

choose.en: I took a taxi from the airport to the hotel.
choose.why: The end destination point takes 까지.

choose.en: I take a rest from Wednesday to Thursday.
choose.why: A time span from Wednesday to Thursday uses the pair 부터 ~ 까지.

fill.en: I go from home to the market.
I am busy from morning to evening.

cards.when: 누구에게 선물이나 물건을 주는지 말할 때
cards.en: I gave a birthday present to my sibling.

cards.when: 누구에게 말을 하거나 묻는지 나타낼 때
cards.en: I told a secret to my friend.

cards.when: 전화나 편지를 보내는 대상을 가리킬 때
cards.en: I made a phone call to Minsu.

cards.when: 학생이나 아이들에게 지식을 가르칠 때
cards.en: The teacher teaches a song to students.

split.en: Sujin sent a letter to a friend.
I gave water to the puppy.
Minsu asked Jiyoung.
I waved my hand to older brother.

choose.en: I gave bread to my friend.
choose.why: Giving something to a person in conversational Korean takes 한테.

choose.en: Please ask Jiyoung.
choose.why: Directing an inquiry to a person takes 한테.

choose.en: I gave candy to my younger sibling.
choose.why: The person receiving the candy takes 한테.

choose.en: Minsu presented flowers to Jiyoung.
choose.why: Subject 민수 takes 가, and recipient 지영 takes 한테.

fill.en: I gave a book to Minsu.
I wrote a letter to older sister.

cards.when: 두 가지 이상의 물건을 대등하게 묶을 때
cards.en: There are apples and pears on the table.

cards.when: 누구와 같이 어떤 행동을 하는지 말할 때
cards.en: I watch a movie with a friend on the weekend.

cards.when: 말할 때 자연스럽게 사물이나 사람을 이을 때
cards.en: I bought bread and milk.

cards.when: 같거나 다름을 견주는 상대를 가리킬 때
cards.ko: 이 옷은 형 옷{과} 색이 같아요.
cards.en: This outfit has the same color as older brother's clothes.

split.en: Minsu walks in the park with a friend.
I drank coffee and water.
I had a chat with Jiyoung.
I bought a notebook and a pencil.

choose.en: I bought watermelon and bananas.
choose.why: 수박 ends in a consonant, so 과.

choose.en: Older brother and younger sibling laugh.
choose.why: 형 ends in a consonant, so 이랑.

choose.en: I played together with my friend on the weekend.
choose.why: Doing an action together with a friend takes 하고.

choose.en: Apples and strawberries, hat and bag.
choose.why: Both 사과 and 모자 end in vowels, so both take 와.

cards.when: 앞 사람의 말에 나도 그렇다고 덧붙일 때
cards.en: I am a student too.

cards.when: 한 가지 외에 다른 것도 더할 때
cards.en: I ate an apple, and I ate a banana too.

cards.when: 다른 사람이나 대상도 같은 행동을 할 때
cards.en: Minsu goes, and Jiyoung goes too.

cards.when: 두 가지 좋은 점을 함께 말할 때
cards.ko: 이 식당은 맛{도} 좋고 값{도} 싸요.
cards.en: This restaurant has good taste and the price is cheap too.

split.en: I like coffee too.
Minsu eats bread too.
Today is warm too.
My younger sibling is kind too.

choose.en: I learn Korean too.
choose.why: Expressing 'me too' takes 도.

choose.en: I sing and dance too.
choose.why: Adding dancing to singing takes 도.

choose.en: Apples are delicious. Strawberries are sweet too.
choose.why: Saying strawberries are sweet as well takes 도.

choose.en: Sujin comes, and Minsu came too.
choose.why: Both Sujin and Minsu coming takes 도 · 도.

cards.when: 다른 것은 빼고 오직 그것 하나만 가리킬 때
cards.en: Only Minsu is in the classroom.

cards.when: 여러 음식 중 한 가지만 고를 때
cards.en: I eat only apples.

cards.when: 조금만 기다려 달라고 부탁할 때
cards.en: Please wait for just five minutes.

cards.when: 다른 사람에게는 비밀로 하고 한 사람에게만 말할 때
cards.en: I will tell only you.

split.en: Only Sujin came to the park.
I drank only water today.
Please give me just one.
My younger sibling reads only comic books.

choose.q: 다른 친구는 안 오고 지영이___ 왔어요.
choose.en: Other friends did not come and only Jiyoung came.
choose.why: Only Jiyoung came, excluding others, so 만.

choose.en: I want to rest just a little.
choose.why: Wanting to rest 'just a little' takes 만.

choose.en: I do not eat meat and eat only vegetables.
choose.why: Eating only vegetables exclusively takes 만.

choose.q: 저는 커피___ 마시고 차는 안 마셔요.
choose.en: I drink only coffee, not tea.
choose.why: 만 means only: coffee and nothing else.

cards.when: 남은 것이 너무 적어서 부족하다고 느낄 때
cards.en: There is nothing but a glass of water.

cards.when: 남은 개수가 하나뿐일 때
cards.en: Only one apple is left.

cards.when: 가진 돈이 너무 모자랄 때
cards.en: I have nothing but 1,000 won in my wallet.

cards.when: 의지할 사람이 오직 한 사람뿐일 때
cards.en: I have nobody but my friend.

split.en: There is only ten minutes left.
There are only two coins in the pocket.
Only three people came to the classroom.
I know only Korean.

choose.en: Only one apple is left.
choose.why: With negative 안 남았어요 expressing shortage, use 밖에.

choose.en: I could only sleep for two hours.
choose.why: With negative verb 못 잤어요 expressing insufficient sleep, use 밖에.

choose.en: I have only 1,000 won in my wallet.
choose.why: With negative 없어요 expressing shortage of money, use 밖에.

choose.q: 교실에 지영 씨___ 민수 씨___ 안 남았어요.
choose.en: In the classroom, only Jiyoung and Minsu are left.
choose.why: Connecting two people with 하고 and expressing scarcity with negative 안 남았어요 takes 하고 · 밖에.

fill.en: I could read only three pages.

cards.when: 둘 중 아무거나 먹고 싶을 때
cards.en: I eat bread or rice.

cards.when: 상대방에게 차나 음료를 권할 때
cards.en: Drink coffee or tea.

cards.when: 약속 날짜를 둘 중 하나로 정할 때
cards.en: Let's meet on Saturday or Sunday.

cards.when: 마땅한 것이 없어 차선책을 고를 때
cards.en: I am bored, shall we watch a movie or something?

split.en: I read a book or newspaper in the morning.
Eat apples or bananas.
I ride a bus or subway.
Sujin went to the market or supermarket.

choose.en: I eat watermelon or Korean melon.
choose.why: 수박 ends in a consonant, so 이나.

choose.en: I drink milk or juice.
choose.why: 우유 ends in a vowel, so 나.

choose.en: Shall we go hiking or something on the weekend?
choose.why: Suggesting an activity casually as an option takes 이나.

choose.en: Wallets or bags, hats or shoes.
choose.why: 지갑 ends in a consonant (이나) and 모자 ends in a vowel (나).

fill.en: Let's watch a movie or something.

cards.when: 먹은 양이 생각보다 많아 놀랄 때
cards.en: I ate as many as three bowls of rice.

cards.when: 모인 사람이 기대보다 훨씬 많을 때
cards.en: As many as ten guests came.

cards.when: 걸린 시간이 너무 길다고 느낄 때
cards.en: I waited for my friend for as long as two hours.

cards.when: 물건값이 예상보다 지나치게 비쌀 때
cards.ko: 사과가 한 개에 오천 원{이나} 해요.
cards.en: Apples cost as much as 5,000 won each.

split.en: Minsu drank as many as four cups of coffee.
Sujin read as many as five books today.
split.ko: 수진은 오늘 책 다섯 권이나 읽었어요.

split.en: I walked as many as ten kilometers in the park.
There are as many as twenty students in the classroom.

choose.en: I bought as many as five apples!
choose.why: 개 ends in a vowel, so 나.

choose.en: I ate as many as seven candies!
choose.why: 알 ends in a consonant, so 이나.

choose.en: I have as much as 100,000 won!
choose.why: Expressing surprise at an unexpectedly large amount takes 이나.

choose.q: 세 잔___ 마시고 두 시간___ 잤어요.
choose.en: I drank as many as three cups and slept for as long as two hours.
choose.why: 잔 and 시간 both end in consonants, taking 이나 · 이나.

fill.en: I ate as many as three.
It takes as long as five hours.
As many as fifty people gathered.

cards.when: 버스나 지하철을 타고 이동할 때
cards.en: I go to school by bus.

cards.when: 어느 언어로 대화하는지 나타낼 때
cards.en: I talk with a friend in Korean.

cards.when: 오른쪽이나 위쪽으로 향할 때
cards.en: Please go to the right.

cards.when: 무엇으로 만들었는지 재료를 밝힐 때
cards.en: I made a chair with wood.

split.en: I write a letter with a pen.
Minsu goes to Seoul by train.
Please come forward slowly.
I cut paper with scissors.

choose.en: I write letters with a pencil.
choose.why: 연필 ends in the consonant ㄹ, so it takes 로.

choose.en: I eat rice with my hands.
choose.why: 손 ends in a consonant other than ㄹ, so 으로.

choose.en: I transfer by subway.
choose.why: Transportation method takes 로.

choose.en: I go by taxi and come by bus.
choose.why: Both 택시 and 버스 end in vowels, taking 로.

cards.when: 정확하지 않고 대략적인 시간을 잡을 때
cards.en: Let's meet around three o'clock.

cards.when: 대략적인 가격을 짐작하여 말할 때
cards.en: It costs about 5,000 won.

cards.when: 물건이나 과일 개수를 어림할 때
cards.en: I bought about five apples.

cards.when: 사람 수를 대략 짐작할 때
cards.en: About twenty people gathered in the playground.

split.en: It takes about thirty minutes from home to school.
Minsu will arrive around two o'clock.
About ten students are in the library.
I read about half of this book.

choose.q: 몇 시___ 만날까요? 한 시쯤 만나요.
choose.en: Around what time shall we meet? Let's meet around one.
choose.why: Asking or stating approximate time takes 쯤.

choose.en: This outfit costs about 10,000 won.
choose.why: Approximating price takes 쯤.

choose.en: Please give me about three apples.
choose.why: Requesting an approximate quantity takes 쯤.

choose.en: Around four o'clock, about five people gather.
choose.why: Both approximate time and headcount take 쯤.

cards.when: 하얗거나 둥근 모양이 비슷할 때
cards.en: The skin is white like snow.

cards.when: 마음이나 장소가 바다처럼 넓을 때
cards.en: The heart is wide like the sea.

cards.when: 선생님이나 부모님을 닮고 싶을 때
cards.en: I want to become a kind person like my teacher.

cards.when: 봄날처럼 따스하고 포근할 때
cards.en: The smile is warm like a spring day.

split.en: Minsu runs fast like a cheetah.
Sujin sings well like a singer.
Water is clear like glass.
The child laughs brightly like an angel.

choose.en: Flowers white like snow bloomed.
choose.why: Resembling snow in whiteness takes 처럼.

choose.en: I look at the sky blue like the sea.
choose.why: Resembling the sea takes 같이.

choose.en: My younger sibling hops like a rabbit.
choose.why: Comparing jumping action to a rabbit takes 처럼.

choose.en: Clear like water and shining like stars.
choose.why: Both comparing resemblance to water and stars take 처럼.

fill.en: She is kind like an angel.
It is wide like the sea.

cards.when: 둘 중 무엇이 더 큰지 견줄 때
cards.en: Watermelons are bigger than apples.

cards.when: 비행기와 기차의 빠르기를 비교할 때
cards.en: Airplanes are faster than trains.

cards.when: 사람의 키나 신체를 견줄 때
cards.en: My older brother is taller than me.

cards.when: 어제와 오늘의 기온을 비교할 때
cards.en: Today is colder than yesterday.

split.en: Trains are faster than buses.
Minsu is bigger than me.
Summer is hotter than spring.
Apples are sweeter than lemons.

choose.en: Older brother is taller than younger sibling.
choose.why: Comparing height against younger sibling takes 보다.

choose.en: Airplanes are much faster than ships.
choose.why: Comparing speed against a ship takes 보다.

choose.en: Today is busier than yesterday.
choose.why: Comparing today's busyness against yesterday takes 보다.

choose.q: 여름은 가을___ 덥고 겨울은 봄___ 추워요.
choose.en: Summer is hotter than autumn, and winter is colder than spring.
choose.why: Comparative statements comparing seasons take 보다 · 보다.

fill.en: It is bigger than an apple.
It is faster than a car.

cards.when: 아침이나 저녁처럼 때마다 반복될 때
cards.en: I exercise every morning.

cards.when: 주말이나 일요일마다 빠짐없이 할 때
cards.en: I go to the library every Sunday.

cards.when: 방마다, 사람마다 모두 그렇다고 할 때
cards.en: Every room has a window.

cards.when: 십 분마다 버스가 올 때
cards.en: The bus comes every ten minutes.

split.en: I write a diary every evening.
Minsu swims every weekend.
Every person has a different face.
The train arrives every thirty minutes.

choose.en: I go jogging every morning.
choose.why: Every morning without exception takes 마다.

choose.en: Every country has a different culture.
choose.why: Every country without exception takes 마다.

choose.en: I meet friends every Saturday.
choose.why: Repeating regularly every Saturday takes 마다.

choose.en: I exercise every Sunday morning.
choose.why: Both Sunday and morning take 마다: every Sunday, every morning.

_note: 조사 블록 구역 자료(단원 id → cards · split · choose · fill · pool). 만드는 법 docs/antigravity/antigravity-particles-blocks-task.md. 안티가 채우고 Claude 가 검토한다. 검사: node tools/check-particles-blocks.mjs

sides.label: 은/는
sides.en: The sky is blue (a general fact, or in contrast).

sides.label: 이/가
sides.en: The sky is blue (I see it now).

sides.label: 은/는
sides.en: As for Minsu, he came.
sides.mean: 민수에 대해 말해요. 다른 사람은 모를 수 있어요.

sides.label: 이/가
sides.en: Minsu is the one who came.

sides.label: 은/는
sides.en: I am a student. (introducing myself)

sides.label: 이/가
sides.en: I am the student. (answer to who)

rule.ko: 「누가 · 뭐가」로 물으면 이/가로 답해요. 이미 알고 있는 것을 말하거나 둘을 견주면 은/는.
rule.en: A who/what question is answered with 이/가. Use 은/는 for what is already known, or to contrast two things.

situations.ctx: 친구가 물어요: 「누가 학생이에요?」
situations.why: A who-question is answered with 이/가.

situations.ctx: 창밖에 갑자기 비가 와요.
situations.why: Something you just noticed takes 이/가.

situations.ctx: 커피와 차를 견주어 말해요.
situations.why: Contrast takes 은/는.

situations.ctx: 처음 만난 사람에게 이름을 말해요.
situations.why: Introducing yourself uses 은/는.

fill2.en: A: What is tasty? B: Kimbap is tasty.
I am a teacher, but my friend is a student.

explain.q: 민수는 왔어요. / 민수가 왔어요. 두 문장은 어떻게 다를까요?
explain.en: Minsu came. How do the two sentences differ?
explain.why: 가 answers who came; 는 talks about Minsu.

sides.label: 은/는
sides.en: Puppies are cute (general fact about puppies).

sides.label: 이/가
sides.en: The puppy is cute (the one I see right now).

sides.label: 은/는
sides.en: Has your sibling come? (we were already talking about them)

sides.label: 이/가
sides.en: Did your sibling come? (checking something new)

sides.label: 은/는
sides.en: Bulgogi is delicious (contrasting with other dishes).

sides.label: 이/가
sides.en: Bulgogi is delicious (answer to what is delicious).

rule.ko: 듣는 사람이 이미 알면 은/는, 새로 보았거나 질문의 답이면 이/가.
rule.en: Use 은/는 when the listener already knows the topic, and 이/가 for new observations or answers to questions.

situations.ctx: 어제 산 새 가방에 대해 친구에게 이야기해요: 「어제 가방을 샀어요.」
situations.why: Once introduced, the bag is now known to both, so use the topic particle 은/는.

situations.ctx: 식당에서 점원이 물어요: 「어느 음식이 매워요?」
situations.why: A which/what question asks for specific identification, answered with 이/가.

situations.ctx: 길을 걷다가 길가에 핀 예쁜 꽃을 발견했어요.
situations.why: Use 이/가 when describing something newly noticed in the moment.

situations.ctx: 한국의 여름 날씨에 대해 일반적인 사실을 말해요.
situations.why: General facts and characteristics of a topic take 은/는.

fill2.en: There is a new building over there.
Korean is fun, but Hanja is difficult.

explain.q: 그 고양이는 작아요. / 그 고양이가 작아요. 두 문장은 맥락이 어떻게 다를까요?
explain.en: That cat is small. How do the two sentences differ in context?
opts: 는: 이미 아는 고양이에 대해 말해요
가: 어느 고양이가 작은지 골라 줘요
explain.why: 은/는 discusses a known cat as the topic, whereas 이/가 picks out which cat is small.

sides.label: 에
sides.en: I am in the park (location of existence).

sides.label: 에서
sides.en: I exercise in the park (location where an action happens).

sides.label: 에
sides.en: I go to the library (destination).

sides.label: 에서
sides.en: I study at the library (location where action takes place).

sides.label: 에
sides.en: I live at home (state of residing).

sides.label: 에서
sides.en: I came out from home (starting point).

rule.ko: 에는 있는 곳 · 가는 곳 · 때, 에서는 일이 일어나는 곳 · 출발점에 씁니다.
rule.en: Use 에 for static location, destination, or time. Use 에서 for dynamic action locations or starting points.

situations.ctx: 친구가 어디 가냐고 물어서 시장으로 향한다고 답해요.
situations.why: Destination with movement verbs like 가다 takes 에.

situations.ctx: 식당 안에서 친구와 맛있는 점심을 먹고 있어요.
situations.why: Eating meal is a dynamic action taking place at a location, requiring 에서.

situations.ctx: 가방이 의자 위에 놓여 있음을 알려 줘요.
situations.why: Existence verbs like 있다 require static location particle 에.

situations.ctx: 아침 일찍 지하철역에서 출발했어요.
situations.why: Starting point of departure takes 에서.

fill2.en: The teacher is in the classroom.

fill2.ko: 오전에 방에 있고 저녁에는 카페에서 쉬어요.
fill2.en: I am in my room in the morning and rest at a cafe in the evening.

explain.q: 카페에 있어요. / 카페에서 만나요. 두 문장의 조사 차이는 무엇일까요?
explain.en: I am at a cafe. / Let us meet at a cafe. What is the difference between the particles?
opts: 에: 머물러 있는 장소, 에서: 만나는 행동이 일어나는 장소
에: 출발하는 곳, 에서: 도착하는 목적지
explain.why: 에 indicates existing in a place, while 에서 marks the venue where an event occurs.

sides.label: 에게/한테
sides.en: I give a present to my younger sibling (receiver is a person).

sides.label: 에
sides.en: I give water to the tree (receiver is a thing/plant).

sides.label: 에게/한테
sides.en: I call my friend (receiver is a person).

sides.label: 에
sides.en: I call the company (receiver is an organization/place).

sides.label: 에게/한테
sides.en: I give a treat to the cat (receiver is an animal).

sides.label: 에
sides.en: I give plant food to the pot (receiver is an inanimate object).

rule.ko: 사람 · 동물에는 에게 · 한테, 물건 · 장소에는 에를 씁니다.
rule.en: Use 에게/한테 for people and animals. Use 에 for objects, plants, and places.

situations.ctx: 친한 친구에게 생일 축하 카드를 보내요.
situations.why: The recipient of the card is a person, taking 한테.

situations.ctx: 베란다 화초에 물을 주는 상황이에요.
situations.why: Plants and inanimate things take 에, not 에게.

situations.ctx: 병원에 진료 예약을 하려고 전화를 걸어요.
situations.why: An institution or facility takes 에.

situations.ctx: 귀여운 강아지에게 맛있는 사료를 줘요.
situations.why: Animals take 에게 or 한테 as living receivers.

fill2.en: I gave a thank-you letter to the teacher.

fill2.ko: 동생한테 과자를 주고 식물에 물을 줬어요.
fill2.en: I gave snacks to my sibling and gave water to the plant.

explain.q: 친구에게 줘요. / 꽃에 물을 줘요. 두 문장의 조사 차이는 무엇일까요?
explain.en: I give it to a friend. / I give water to a flower. What is the difference in particles?
opts: 받는 쪽이 사람이면 에게, 식물이나 사물이면 에
받는 쪽이 장소면 에게, 사람이면 에
explain.why: Living persons and animals take 에게/한테, while non-human objects and plants take 에.

sides.label: 로
sides.en: I go by taxi (ends in a vowel → 로).
sides.mean: 받침 없는 말 뒤에 로를 써요.

sides.label: 으로
sides.en: I move it by truck (ends in a consonant other than ㄹ → 으로).

sides.label: 로
sides.en: I cut with a knife (ends in ㄹ → 로).

sides.label: 으로
sides.en: I hold it with my hand (ends in consonant ㄴ → 으로).

sides.label: 로
sides.en: I depart toward Seoul (ends in ㄹ → 로).

sides.label: 으로
sides.en: Head toward the right (ends in consonant ㄱ → 으로).

rule.ko: (으)로는 도구 · 수단 · 방향에 써요. 모음이나 ㄹ 받침 뒤에는 로, 그 밖의 받침 뒤에는 으로.
rule.en: (으)로 expresses tool, transport, or direction. Use 로 after vowels or ㄹ, and 으로 after all other consonants.

situations.ctx: 친구가 연필을 쥐고 편지를 써요.
situations.why: 연필 ends in batchim ㄹ, so it takes 로.

situations.ctx: 지하철을 타고 출근해요.
situations.why: 지하철 ends in batchim ㄹ, so it takes 로.

situations.ctx: 젓가락을 사용해서 음식을 먹어요.
situations.why: 젓가락 ends in consonant ㄱ, which takes 으로.

situations.ctx: 길 안내를 하며 왼쪽 방향을 가리켜요.
situations.why: 왼쪽 ends in consonant ㄱ, so it takes 으로.

fill2.en: I pasted the photo with glue.

fill2.ko: 비행기로 제주도에 가고 배로 섬을 돌아요.
fill2.en: I go to Jeju Island by plane and tour the island by boat.

explain.q: 연필로 써요. / 손으로 써요. 조사의 모양이 왜 다를까요?
explain.en: I write with a pencil. / I write with my hand. Why do the particle shapes differ?
opts: ㄹ 받침은 로를 쓰고, 다른 자음 받침은 으로를 써요
사람 손에는 로를 쓰고, 물건에는 으로를 써요
explain.why: Words ending in ㄹ take 로, while words ending in other consonants take 으로.

sides.label: 와/과
sides.en: I eat with a friend (written/formal, vowel ending → 와).

sides.label: 하고
sides.en: I eat with a friend (neutral, most common).

sides.label: (이)랑
sides.en: I eat with a friend (spoken/casual, vowel ending → 랑).

sides.label: 와/과
sides.en: I play with my younger sibling (written/formal, consonant ending → 과).

sides.label: 하고
sides.en: I play with my younger sibling (neutral, unchanged).

sides.label: (이)랑
sides.en: I play with my younger sibling (spoken/casual, consonant ending → 이랑).

sides.label: 와/과
sides.en: I bought apples and bananas (written/formal, vowel ending → 와).

sides.label: 하고
sides.en: I bought apples and bananas (neutral).

sides.label: (이)랑
sides.en: I bought apples and bananas (spoken).

rule.ko: 와/과는 격식체 글, 하고는 일상 표현, (이)랑은 친한 대화에서 써요. 하고는 모양이 바뀌지 않아요.
rule.en: 와/과 is formal/written, 하고 is neutral everyday, and (이)랑 is spoken casual. 하고 never changes form.

situations.ctx: 공식 안내문에 부모님과 함께 참석한다는 문장을 적어요.
situations.why: In formal written contexts, 과 (after consonant) is preferred over the casual 이랑.

situations.ctx: 친한 동생에게 편하게 말하며 같이 가자고 해요.
situations.why: In spoken casual speech after a vowel, 랑 is used. (나 takes 와 in formal).

situations.ctx: 받침 유무와 상관없이 항상 똑같은 모양으로 쓰고 싶어요.
situations.why: 하고 never changes its form regardless of whether there is a final consonant.

situations.ctx: 책상 위에 연필과 지우개가 함께 놓여 있음을 글로 써요.
situations.why: Words ending in a consonant take 과.

fill2.ko: 빵하고 우유를 사고 주스랑 과자도 먹었어요.
fill2.en: I bought bread and milk, and also had juice and snacks.

explain.q: 친구와 만나요. / 친구랑 만나요. 두 문장의 어감 차이는 무엇일까요?
explain.en: I meet with a friend. What is the difference in nuance?
opts: 와: 격식 있는 글 표현, 랑: 편한 대화 표현
와: 혼자 행동함, 랑: 여럿이 행동함
explain.why: 와/과 is formal and literary, whereas (이)랑 is informal and conversational.

sides.label: 도
sides.en: I drink water too (in addition to something else).

sides.label: 만
sides.en: I only drink water (nothing else).

sides.label: 밖에
sides.en: I drink nothing but water (negative expression).

sides.label: 도
sides.en: Minsu came too (along with other people).

sides.label: 만
sides.en: Only Minsu came (nobody else came).

sides.label: 밖에
sides.en: Nobody came except Minsu (negative expression).

sides.label: 도
sides.en: I have 1,000 won too (in addition to other money).
sides.mean: 다른 돈과 함께 천 원도 있어요.

sides.label: 만
sides.en: I only have 1,000 won (positive sentence with only).

sides.label: 밖에
sides.en: I have nothing but 1,000 won (negative verb 없어요).

rule.ko: 도는 또한, 만은 오직 하나, 밖에는 뒤에 반드시 부정어(없다 · 안 · 못)가 와요.
rule.en: 도 means also, 만 means only, and 밖에 means nothing but and must pair with a negative word (없다, 안, 못).

situations.ctx: 지갑에 오직 동전 하나만 남아 있고 더는 없어요: 「동전 하나___ 없어요.」
situations.why: When followed by the negative verb 없어요 expressing shortage/exclusivity, use 밖에.

situations.ctx: 선생님께서 다른 학생뿐 아니라 나에게도 질문을 하셨어요.
situations.why: Use 도 to mean also/too in addition to others.

situations.ctx: 긍정 문장으로 오직 사과 한 개만 먹었다고 말해요: 「사과 하나___ 먹었어요.」
situations.why: 만 can be used with positive verbs like 먹었어요, whereas 밖에 requires a negative verb.

situations.ctx: 모임에 열 명을 초대했는데 한 명 말고는 오지 않았어요.
situations.why: 한 명밖에 안 왔어요 means only one person came (excluding that one, nobody came).

fill2.en: Only two people are left in the classroom.

fill2.ko: 교실에 지수만 남고 민수도 집에 갔어요.
fill2.en: Only Jisu stayed in the classroom, and Minsu went home too.

explain.q: 물만 있어요. / 물밖에 없어요. 두 문장의 문법적인 차이는 무엇일까요?
explain.en: I only have water. What is the grammatical difference?
opts: 만은 긍정 서술어와 쓰고, 밖에는 부정 서술어와 써요
만은 사람에게만 쓰고, 밖에는 사물에만 써요
explain.why: 만 works with positive verbs like 있어요, while 밖에 requires negative words like 없어요.

title.ko: 녹차 ○ 홍차를 마셔요 vs 귤을 여섯 개 ○ 먹었어요

sides.label: 선택 (또는)
sides.en: I drink green tea or black tea (choice between two options).

sides.label: 많음 (놀람)
sides.en: I ate as many as six tangerines (more than expected).

title.ko: 금요일 ○ 토요일 vs 네 시간 ○ 기다렸어요

sides.label: 선택 (또는)
sides.en: Let us meet on Friday or Saturday (choice of day).

sides.label: 많음 (놀람)
sides.en: I waited for as long as four hours (surprisingly long time).

title.ko: 책 ○ 영화 vs 열 권 ○ 읽었어요

sides.label: 선택 (또는)
sides.en: I read a book or watch a movie (choice of activity).

sides.label: 많음 (놀람)
sides.en: I read as many as ten books (large quantity).

rule.ko: (이)나는 둘 중 하나를 고르는 「또는」과, 많아서 놀랍다는 느낌을 더하는 두 가지 뜻이 있어요.
rule.en: (이)나 has two uses: "or" between two choices, and adding surprise that an amount is large.

situations.ctx: 식당에서 음료수를 고르며 콜라 또는 주스를 달라고 해요.
situations.why: (이)나 means 'or' when choosing between items.

situations.ctx: 친구가 밥을 무려 네 그릇을 먹어서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
situations.why: Use (이)나 attached to a quantity to express that the amount is surprisingly large.

situations.ctx: 받침 있는 명사(책) 뒤에 선택을 붙이려고 해요.
situations.why: Words ending in a consonant take 이나.

situations.ctx: 모임에 예상보다 훨씬 많은 스무 명이 왔어요.
situations.why: (이)나 expresses that twenty people is an unexpectedly large turnout.

fill2.en: Shall we eat pizza or hamburgers?

fill2.ko: 주말에 산책이나 운동을 하고 물을 두 병이나 마셨어요.
fill2.en: I took a walk or exercised on the weekend and drank as many as two bottles of water.

explain.q: 사과나 배를 먹어요. / 사과를 다섯 개나 먹어요. 두 문장의 (이)나의 뜻은 어떻게 다를까요?
explain.en: How do the meanings of (이)나 differ in these two sentences?
opts: 첫 번째는 선택(또는), 두 번째는 생각보다 많은 수량(무려)
첫 번째는 함께, 두 번째는 장소
explain.why: Between nouns, (이)나 means 'or'; attached to numbers/counters, it emphasizes a surprisingly large quantity.

sides.label: 장소 (에서)
sides.en: I walk from home to school (place starting point → 에서).

sides.label: 시간 (부터)
sides.en: I work from 9 o'clock to 6 o'clock (time starting point → 부터).

sides.label: 장소 (에서)
sides.en: I go from Seoul to Busan (places).

sides.label: 시간 (부터)
sides.en: I study from Monday to Friday (days/times).

sides.label: 장소 (에서)
sides.en: I ride a bicycle from the station to the park.

sides.label: 시간 (부터)
sides.en: It rains from morning to evening.

rule.ko: 장소의 출발점에는 에서 ~ 까지, 시간의 시작점에는 부터 ~ 까지를 씁니다.
rule.en: Use 에서 ~ 까지 for places (from place A to place B), and 부터 ~ 까지 for times (from time X to time Y).

situations.ctx: 집에서 출발하여 회사까지 걸어가는 거리를 이야기해요: 「집___ 회사까지 걸어요.」
situations.why: From a starting place, use 에서 with 까지.

situations.ctx: 수업이 시작하는 시간이 오후 두 시예요: 「두 시___ 네 시까지 수업이에요.」
situations.why: From a starting time point, use 부터 with 까지.

situations.ctx: 내일부터 주말까지 방학이에요: 「내일___ 일요일까지 쉬어요.」
situations.why: 내일 is a time point, pairing with 부터.

situations.ctx: 공항에서 호텔까지 택시를 타고 가요: 「공항___ 호텔까지 택시를 타요.」
situations.why: 공항 is a physical location, so use 에서.

fill2.en: I travel from Incheon to Jeju Island by boat.

fill2.ko: 오전부터 밤까지 공부하고 도서관에서 집까지 걸었어요.
fill2.en: I studied from morning to night and walked from the library to home.

explain.q: 집에서 학교까지 / 1시부터 3시까지 두 표현에서 에서와 부터의 차이는 무엇일까요?
explain.en: What is the difference between 에서 and 부터 in these expressions?
opts: 에서는 장소의 출발점, 부터는 시간의 시작점
에서는 사람의 출발점, 부터는 사물의 시작점
explain.why: 에서 pairs with physical places (from place A), whereas 부터 pairs with temporal points (from time X).

choose.q: A: 누가 지민이에요? B: 수진 씨___ 지민이에요.
choose.en: A: Who is Jimin? B: Sujin is Jimin.
choose.why: Questions asking 'who' (누가) are answered with 이/가.

choose.q: A: 무엇을 마셔요? B: 물___ 마셔요.
choose.en: A: What do you drink? B: I drink water.
choose.why: 물 ends with a consonant (ㄹ 받침), so the object particle 을 is used.

choose.en: These are Minsu's glasses.
choose.why: 의 marks possession (Minsu's).

choose.en: Apples are cheap. But strawberries are expensive.
choose.why: Contrast between two subjects requires 은/는. 딸기 ends in a vowel, taking 는.

choose.en: Jiyoung washes an apple.
choose.why: 사과 is the object and ends in a vowel, taking 를.

choose.en: As for today, the weather is really warm.
choose.why: 오늘 sets the general topic of the sentence, taking 은.

fix.en: My head hurts.
My younger sibling drinks milk.
The teacher's bag is heavy.
This book is my sibling's book.

choose.en: We took photos in the park.
choose.why: Taking photos is an action taking place in a location, requiring 에서 (common mistake: using 에 for place of action).

choose.en: The class begins from 9 a.m.
choose.why: Starting point in time requires 부터 (common mistake: using 에서 for time).

choose.en: I gave a birthday gift to Sujin.
choose.why: Giving something to a person requires 에게 or 한테, not 에.

choose.en: I go to my parents' home on weekends.
choose.why: Destination of a movement verb like 가다 takes 에.

choose.en: I learned Korean from a friend.
choose.why: Receiving or learning from a person takes 한테 or 에게.

choose.en: It takes ten minutes on foot to Seoul Station.
choose.why: 까지 indicates the arrival limit or destination (up to / until).

fix.en: I eat lunch at the restaurant.
I walk from home to the library.
I send a letter to a friend.
I study from one o'clock to three o'clock.

fill.en: There is money inside the wallet.
Please submit your homework by tomorrow.
It has been raining since morning.

choose.en: I have nothing but one ballpoint pen in the drawer.
choose.why: 밖에 requires a negative ending like 없어요 (common mistake: using 만 with negative when meaning 'nothing but').

choose.en: I drank as many as four cups of coffee over the weekend.
choose.why: 이나 expresses that an amount is unexpectedly large (as many as).

choose.en: There are bread and milk on the table.
choose.why: 빵 ends with a consonant (ㅇ 받침), so 과 is used.

choose.en: My younger sibling came, and my friend came too.
choose.why: 도 means 'also' or 'too'.

choose.en: Yesterday I watched a movie with my older sister.
choose.why: 언니 ends in a vowel, so 랑 is attached directly.

choose.en: Only Minsu remained in the classroom.
choose.why: 만 means 'only', emphasizing exclusivity with an affirmative verb.

fix.en: I only listen to Korean songs.
There are apples and bananas in the bag.
Yesterday I went shopping with Sujin.
I have nothing but one coin in my pocket.

fill.en: Today I will only drink tea.
There is nothing but water in the fridge.
Shall we take a walk or something this weekend?

choose.en: I go to City Hall by subway.
choose.why: 지하철 ends in ㄹ 받침, so it takes 로 (common mistake: using 으로 after ㄹ).

choose.en: Korean is more difficult than English.
choose.why: 보다 is attached to the baseline noun in a comparison (more than English).

choose.en: I go jogging every morning.
choose.why: 마다 means 'every' (every morning).

choose.en: I meet my friend around three o'clock at the station.
choose.why: 쯤 indicates approximation of time or amount (around 3 o'clock).

choose.en: Jiyoung is cute like a doll.
choose.why: 처럼 expresses resemblance or likeness (like a doll).

choose.en: I eat soup with a spoon.
choose.why: 숟가락 ends in a consonant (ㄱ 받침), taking 으로 for the tool.

fix.en: I write letters with a pencil.
We go on a trip by bus.
Sujin goes to church every Sunday.
My older brother is brave like a tiger.

fill.en: An airplane is much faster than a ship.
Every country has a different culture.

choose.en: I return the book to the library.
choose.why: 도서관 is a place or institution, taking 에 rather than 에게 (people/animals).

choose.en: I ride the KTX from Seoul to Busan.
choose.why: Starting point for physical journey between places takes 에서, not 부터.

choose.en: My younger sibling is sleeping in the room right now.
choose.why: Sleeping is an activity occurring at a location, requiring 에서.

choose.q: A: 누가 전화했어요? B: 민수___ 전화했어요.
choose.en: A: Who called? B: Minsu called.
choose.why: Answers to who-questions focus on the subject with 이/가.

choose.en: There is nothing left in the fridge except one bottle of milk.
choose.why: When paired with a negative verb (안 남았어요), 밖에 expresses 'nothing but'.

choose.en: I eat rice with a spoon.
choose.why: 으로 indicates the instrument used for eating.

fix.en: I sent a birthday celebration message to a friend.
I take classes starting from nine in the morning.
The basement is cool, but the rooftop is warm.
If you are thirsty, drink juice or tea.

fill.en: A pencil is placed on the desk.
I picked clothes at the department store.
My older brother plays soccer well.
As for me, I rest at home on weekends.

choose.en: I gave a gift to my grandmother.
choose.why: 께 is the honorific recipient particle used for elders such as grandmother.

choose.en: In summer, the days are longer than in winter.
choose.why: 겨울 takes 보다 for the comparison standard (longer than winter).

choose.en: People lined up at every bus stop.
choose.why: 마다 means 'every' (at each bus stop).

choose.en: We went to Jeju Island by plane.
choose.why: 비행기 ends in a vowel, so 로 is used for the means of transport.

choose.q: A: 어디___ 아파요? B: 배가 아파요.
choose.en: A: Where hurts? B: My stomach hurts.
choose.why: Question words like 어디 take 이/가.

choose.en: After the meal, I drink warm tea.
choose.why: 차 ends in a vowel, so it takes the object particle 를.

fix.en: Children touch sand with their hands.
I asked the teacher about a difficult question.
I like my friend's gift.
Yesterday I rode a bicycle with a friend in the park.

fill.en: There is a clock inside the classroom.
We share conversations at the cafe.
I read the newspaper every morning.
In the evening, I watch an exciting movie.
